newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Long bond yields spiked higher during the day but managed to hold below the key 15.40 percent level in trade characterised by local and offshore selling, bond traders said.
At 1415 GMT the yield on the benchmark R150 stock was at 15.38 percent from 15.28 percent at 1400 GMT on Friday after meeting resistance at 15.40 percent.

Traders said the yield on the benchmark R150 stock climbed rapidly after the official opening on the back of negative sentiment over the September gold and forex reserves figure released late on Friday.
"The fact that the Reserve Bank drew 612 million rand in foreign credit lines over the month-end was not interpreted as positive," one trader said.

South Africa's combined gold and foreign exchange reserves fell 35.68 million rand in September to 10.04 billion rand from August's 10.08 billion rand, when they fell 292.1 million rand, Reserve Bank figures released late on Friday showed.
The bank said that foreign credit lines amounting to 612 million rand were utilised over the month-end.
Traders said the key 15.37 percent level was quickly broken but good support emerged at the 15.40 percent level.
A negative August producer price index figure, due out on Tuesday at 0900 GMT, had already been discounted and would only move the market if it was significantly out of forecast ranges.
According to a Reuters consensus poll of 10 economists, PPI would rise 7.2 percent year-on-year and 0.9 percent month-on-month, compared with a 6.6 and 0.8 percent rise in August.
Bond Exchange figures show foreigners bought a net 3.84 million rand worth of South African bonds on Friday after buying 188.68 million rand worth of South African bonds on Thursday.
Nominal cumulative volumes amounted to 4.36 billion rand on Friday from 35.39 billion rand on Thursday -- a settlement day.
The rand ended a slow day slightly firmer on the dollar at 4.5315/5365 from 4.5350/5400 on Friday.
Dealers said the market was caught long on dollars late on Friday ahead of the reserves figure and early position-squaring saw the rand drift stronger.
"The currency then drifted in a narrow 4.5310 to 4.5340 range in slow two-way trade for the rest of the day," a dealer at one of South Africa's big local banks said.
"There was not much going on...the short-term 4.52 to 4.54 range is still intact as is the broader 4.5050 to 4.5450 range," the dealer said.
Other traders noted that trade had been relatively quiet and the rand had not been much influenced by the weaker bond market.
Against the crosses the rand was last trading at 7.0912/1022 from 7.0997/1074 on Friday and was at 0.3370/3375 marks from 0.3367/3372 marks previously.
On the money market, three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.75 and 15.95 percent, while 90-day BAs were unchanged in a 15.20-15.35 percent band.
The daily shortage fell below the nine billion mark to be quoted at 8.032 billion rand on Saturday from 8.042 billion rand on Friday.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
